title: Schema validator now checks schemas with the correct metaschema path
summary: Resolved. The strict validator now uses the proper jsonschema schema check path, so the archive no longer shows the broken metaschema behavior.
evidence: The repaired validator was run against the archive and passed 425/425 checks. The transcript calls this the cleanest completed fix in the archive.
why_it_matters: A broken validator makes every downstream schema gate suspect and can hide real doc or artifact drift.
recommended_action: Keep the fix, then add regression coverage so strict mode cannot regress silently.
resolution: Switched schema self-validation to jsonschema.Draft7Validator.check_schema(data) and reran the validator successfully.

title: Strict schema validator still lacks regression tests
summary: Open. The validator is fixed, but strict-mode still lacks dedicated regression coverage for the known-valid and known-invalid schema cases.
evidence: The transcript says the repaired validator passed, but no new regression test was added in the archive.
why_it_matters: Without coverage, the old bad behavior can return without an obvious signal.
recommended_action: Add tests for valid schema pass, invalid schema fail, and inventory-wide strict validation.

title: AgentLoop extraction still depends on façade backreferences
summary: Open. The new runtime modules exist, but AgentLoop still owns the original mixins and the runtime adapters still reach back into the full façade.
evidence: AgentLoop still inherits the original operational mixins, and ToolRuntimeAdapterBuilder still receives the full loop object rather than a typed dependency port.
why_it_matters: Hidden backreferences preserve coupling and make ownership boundaries ambiguous.
recommended_action: Replace façade backreferences with typed ports and finish the extraction only after the port-based path is covered.

title: ModelRuntime snapshots session metadata at construction
summary: Open. ModelRuntime stores session, parent-session, prompt, and message identifiers once during construction and later reuses those frozen values when building request metadata.
evidence: The runtime keeps _session_id, _parent_session_id, _is_user_prompt_call, and _current_user_message_id as private fields and uses them in build_request_metadata().
why_it_matters: A later session reset or fork can leave requests correlated to stale turn metadata.
recommended_action: Pull metadata from live turn state or a typed context port instead of constructor-time snapshots.

title: Failed tool resolution can short-circuit into final assistant output
summary: Open. The batch result path treats failed tool calls as part of the assistant turn instead of routing them through a distinct failure continuation.
evidence: get_turn_batch_result() uses assistant_is_final = not has_tool_calls and not has_failed, so a turn with only failed calls can look complete.
why_it_matters: Unresolved tool requests can be dropped instead of producing the failure path the model and user need to see.
recommended_action: Split the continuation contract into valid tool batch, failed tool batch, and final assistant output.

title: Governed context injection still lacks direct contract tests
summary: Open. ContextRuntime now injects governed context into the model-visible message stream, but the archive does not contain a direct test proving the injected sequence, receipt binding, or cross-turn deduplication.
evidence: The runtime builds a governed prompt, inserts it as a system message, and records a receipt, but no dedicated test covers that flow end to end.
why_it_matters: Without a contract test, the governed context path can silently drift or duplicate across turns.
recommended_action: Add a model-facing test that asserts message order, receipt fields, and non-duplication across repeated turns.

title: Tool result cache still falls back to ambient cwd and package-local storage
summary: Open. The cache API accepts workspace_root, but the adapter path still omits it and the cache root still resolves under rig_relay/.build/rig-relay/tool-cache/.
evidence: get_cached_result() and set_cached_result() default to Path.cwd() when workspace_root is not passed, and BUILD_ROOT is derived from the package path.
why_it_matters: Cross-worktree cache collisions and source-tree cache residue remain possible.
recommended_action: Pass explicit workspace identity through the cache adapters and relocate the cache outside the package tree.

title: Generated-code compiler still accepts unsafe arbitrary input forms
summary: Open. The compiler path still allows arbitrary dict input and template substitution, and the validator imports candidate code before any AST allowlist can reject it.
evidence: The generator still accepts model_spec as dict or template_path overrides, and the validator still reaches spec.loader.exec_module(mod) early in the flow.
why_it_matters: Autonomous or promoted execution can still generate and import attacker-shaped Python.
recommended_action: Constrain the IR, remove arbitrary template selection from promoted paths, inspect AST before import, and quarantine execution for real.

title: Static site renderer still has unsafe JSON-LD and disclosure seams
summary: Open. The renderer path still needs a fail-closed validator stance, safer structured-data serialization, URL-scheme checks, and a disclosure fix for the telemetry copy.
evidence: The transcript reproduced a script-tag breakout in structured data, noted that missing jsonschema currently returns success, and called out the public "No tracking" disclosure as false.
why_it_matters: Public docs can emit unsafe HTML or describe product behavior incorrectly.
recommended_action: Fail closed on validator absence, serialize structured data through a safe script-context boundary, validate URLs, and correct the disclosure text.

title: Telemetry mode vocabulary still splits across runtime, profile, and projection
summary: Open. The telemetry default-on change landed, but the profile, projection, and client layers still disagree on mode names and on what no-profile means.
evidence: Projection code emits enabled_first_party and disabled_by_user, while telemetry send code still returns disabled/degraded/full and the no-profile state still reports disabled.
why_it_matters: Users and tests cannot rely on one canonical telemetry state model.
recommended_action: Define one enum, wire all projections to it, and make the disclosure surfaces match the same contract.

title: Steward leaves partial claims behind on failure paths
summary: Open. The steward now blocks some bad dispatches, but successful task claims are not released when later reservation or launch steps fail, and dry-run semantics still read like dispatch.
evidence: The transcript notes a claim succeeds before path reservation can fail, and a later try_launch() failure leaves the partial state behind. It also calls out event ordering and dry-run dispatch semantics.
why_it_matters: Leaked claims and ambiguous dispatch events poison the coordination ledger.
recommended_action: Rollback claims on downstream failure, clean up reserved paths on launch refusal, and separate preview events from real dispatches.

title: ConversationRuntime parity test still protects the old architecture
summary: Open. The current parity test asserts the pre-refactor ownership model even though production now dispatches through get_turn_batch_result() and execute_tool_batch().
evidence: The test's source-inspection assertion matches the old adapter story, not the current production flow.
why_it_matters: A fake-green test suite can hide real regressions and block the right follow-up work.
recommended_action: Rewrite or delete the test so it asserts the current production path instead of the obsolete adapter contract.
